title: Clock page — wallpaper window variants
question: Clock page kept, per your steer: smaller time, favorites bottom-aligned, the middle of the screen left empty as wallpaper space. Four ways to arrange that frame. Pick one, steer again, or mix.

options.label: Clock · Corner
options.lineage: teletext page corner — the index lives in the corner, the picture keeps the page
options.thesis: Time tucked top-left, favorites pinned to the floor, the whole middle left to the wallpaper.
options.viewport: 80px yellow 21:47 top-left with a micro date line; six numbered blocks bottom-aligned as a floor rail; colour keys and P110 as one thin line at the very foot; vast empty middle for the wallpaper.
options.risk: Corner-quiet: nothing pulls the eye if the wallpaper is busy behind the blocks.

options.label: Clock · Split rule
options.lineage: teletext page sections divided by single-line headings
options.thesis: One cyan rule across the empty middle divides time-above from favorites-below — the rule itself carries the P110 cue.
materials: inline page cue on the rule
options.viewport: 96px white clock top-left; a thin cyan line across mid-page carrying P110 INPUTS ▸ at its far end; favorites bottom-aligned; keys bottom-left.
options.risk: The middle line competes with the wallpaper it frames.

options.label: Clock · Newsflash
options.lineage: teletext newsflash strips running through page body
options.thesis: The empty middle gets exactly one line of live state — a newsflash strip that changes, everything else stays out of the wallpaper's way.
options.viewport: Small 64px clock + date inline top-left; one white micro line through mid-page carrying live input or new-content state; favorites bottom rail; keys at foot.
options.risk: The strip must actually carry news — a static line reads as junk chrome.

options.label: Clock · Page frame
options.lineage: full teletext page geometry — every index element in a page corner
options.thesis: The UI becomes a picture frame: clock corner, P100 label corner, favorites floor, keys foot — wallpaper gets the entire centre.
options.viewport: 90px clock top-left, P100 label top-right, six-block favorites rail on the floor, keys bottom-left, P110 bottom-right; nothing else exists between.
options.risk: Maximum wallpaper freedom also means zero hierarchy — all corners compete equally.
